candidates.label: Temple Mount
candidates.support: Wikidata's point for the Temple Mount is corroborated by scholarly archaeological reconstruction of the platform published by Ritmeyer; as a roughly 15-hectare platform, any single point is a center reference rather than a precise boundary.

summary.text: The Temple Mount is the elevated platform in Jerusalem's Old City that carried Herod the Great's expanded Second Temple, the building the Gospels describe Jesus visiting, teaching in, and, in one episode, driving merchants and money changers from.

history.text: Herod the Great began a major expansion and rebuilding of the Second Temple and its surrounding platform around 20-19 BC, a project that, per the Gospel of John, was still being completed decades into the first century AD.
The Temple was destroyed by Roman forces in AD 70, leaving the retaining walls of Herod's platform, including the section known today as the Western Wall, as its most substantial surviving remains.

The seven scripture references below are a representative sample of Gospel and Acts episodes set at the Temple precinct, not an exhaustive list of every New Testament mention of 'the temple,' a phrase that recurs well over one hundred times across the Gospels and Acts.

They came to Jerusalem, and Jesus entered into the temple and began to throw out those who sold and those who bought in the temple, and overthrew the money changers’ tables and the seats of those who sold the doves.
